chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Wasi', from Ismail ibn Sahl, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) left Medina during the remaining days of Sha'ban, so he was fasting. Then the month of Ramadan entered upon him while he was traveling, so he broke his fast. It was said to him, 'You fast Sha'ban and break your fast in the month of Ramadan?' He said, 'Yes. Sha'ban is up to me; if I will, I fast, and if I will, I do not; and the month of Ramadan is a fixed determination from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon me to break the fast.'

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: Travel/Journey (a state that permits shortening prayers and breaking fast)
key_terms.رَمَضَانُ: Ramadan (the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, month of obligatory fasting)
key_terms.شَعْبَانُ: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar)
key_terms.عَزْمٌ: Fixed determination/Command (indicating an obligatory ruling rather than a choice)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Imam fast in Sha'ban but break his fast in Ramadan while traveling?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the jurisprudential distinction between the flexibility of voluntary fasting in Sha'ban and the mandatory nature of breaking fast while traveling during Ramadan. This narration underscores that while personal discretion governs optional acts, the divine command (‘azm) for travelers to break their fast is obligatory, reflecting the principle of ease in Islamic law. It serves as a foundational proof for the permissibility and obligation of breaking the fast during travel in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Wasi’a, from Ismail Bin Sahl, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> went out from Al-Medina during a few remaining days from Shaban, so he<sup>asws</sup> was Fasting. Then the Month of Ramazan entered upon him<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> was in a journey. So it was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> are Fasting Shaban and are breaking (not Fasting) the Month of Ramazan?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. Shabaan to me<sup>asws</sup>, if I<sup>asws</sup> so desire to I<sup>asws</sup> Fast, and if I<sup>asws</sup> so desire to I<sup>asws</sup> don’t; and the Month of Ramazan is a fixed Determination from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic upon me<sup>asws</sup> for the breaking (during a journey)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Mansur ibn al-‘Abbas from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Wash from ‘Isma‘il ibn Sahl from a man who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, commenced a journey just a few days before the end of the month of al-Sha‘ban and he (the Imam) was fasting. The month of Ramadan then started while he (the Imam) was still on his journey but he stopped fasting. He (the Imam) was asked, ‘How is it that you have been fasting in the month of al-Sha‘ban and stopped fasting in the month of Ramadan?’

He (the Imam) said, ‘In the case of the month of al-Sha‘ban it is up to me to fast or not to fast: however, in the case of the month of Ramadan it is the commandment of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, to stop fasting (on a journey).’”
